question: When can a group be embedded in a finitely presented simple group?
idea: The word problem asks whether a string of generators represents the identity. The manuscript claims a finitely generated group has a decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in some finitely presented simple group. The equivalence concerns existence of an algorithm, not a uniform efficient running time.
why: The study of symmetry and reversible operations. A group records how operations combine, such as rotations of a shape.

exactClaim: A finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, proving the Boone–Higman conjecture. The target can have type F∞: a classifying space with finitely many cells in each dimension. A single group of type F∞ can also contain every finitely presented group. )
